show-tanya-ransom.bio: Kimberley/South West songwriter Tanya Ransom blends folk, blues and alt-country with story-led writing, powerful vocals and understated rhythm guitar.
show-tanya-ransom.why: Less aligned with your heavier side, but strong if you want to study mature songwriting, narrative structure and emotional delivery.

show-figurehead.bio: Fremantle five-piece FIGUREHEAD combine alternative rock with contemporary indie pop, groove-led songwriting and polished band production.
show-figurehead.why: Worth seeing for tight band chemistry, arrangement and production ideas; a useful bridge between your rock and pop-writing interests.

show-jack-hamilton.bio: Perth multi-instrumentalist Jack Hamilton builds emotionally charged rock around soaring melodies, raw lyricism and a cathartic live-band sound.
show-jack-hamilton.why: A strong fit for your interest in anthemic rock, multi-instrumental songwriting and arrangements that build toward emotional release.

show-taija.bio: Boorloo artist TAIJA is a young Indigenous hip-hop songwriter whose recent work combines confident rap delivery, R&B melody and polished contemporary production.
show-taija.why: Not a genre match to your heavier material, but useful for vocal production, beat construction and modern hook-writing.

show-maatakitj.bio: Nyoongar songmaker Maatakitj fuses Indigenous song traditions from WA's deep south with desert-blues guitar and electronic/dance ideas. His work also spans collaborations with Kronos Quartet, Angélique Kidjo and Paul Mac.
show-maatakitj.why: One of the best creative fits for you: unusual composition, cultural storytelling, genre fusion and a willingness to move well outside conventional band formats.

show-rosalie-chilvers.bio: Perth pop-rock artist Rosalie Chilvers is known for autobiographical songwriting and a high-energy live show built around big vocals, crowd engagement and punk-pop momentum.
show-rosalie-chilvers.why: Strong fit if you want to watch how personal songs are turned into large, anthemic live moments; useful for your own pop-rock material and stagecraft.

show-stow.bio: Hannah STOW blends indie rock and pop with confessional lyrics, big choruses, occasional electronic production and a direct, charismatic live style.
show-stow.why: Useful for studying lyrical immediacy, audience connection and how pop writing can retain distorted guitars and emotional weight.

show-birdland.bio: Birdland are Perth triplet brothers making sunlit indie-pop with tight musicianship, youthful band chemistry and increasingly polished songwriting.
show-birdland.why: A lighter fit musically, but interesting for natural band interplay, efficient songwriting and seeing how a young act builds a strong live identity.

show-oakabella-mae.bio: Oakabella Mae is a Boorloo/Walyalup singer-songwriter combining introspective folk writing with unusual tunings, experimental arrangement and emotionally detailed storytelling.
show-oakabella-mae.why: A good counterpoint to the heavy acts: especially relevant for your interest in composition, arrangement and songs that can move beyond obvious genre labels.

show-ivory-dusk.bio: Albany heavy-rock band Ivory Dusk combine melodic vocals with heavy guitars and progressive dynamics, citing influences including A Perfect Circle, System Of A Down and Deftones.
show-ivory-dusk.why: Top recommendation. Their progressive, melodic and heavy approach is directly aligned with your preference for dark, big, riff-driven and prog-like music.

show-soul-insync.bio: Brazil-born, Perth-based artist/producer Soul inSync works across R&B, pop, funk and contemporary beat-driven production, pairing melodic hooks with self-produced arrangements.
show-soul-insync.why: More useful as a production reference than a direct genre match; listen for beat choices, vocal layering and how he builds tracks as an artist-producer.

show-boox-kid.bio: Noongar artist Jarred Wall performs as Boox Kid, combining dreamy electronic pop with songwriting, production and sound design. His wider work spans theatre and Noongar-language opera.
show-boox-kid.why: Very strong fit for your wider creative interests: cross-genre writing, production, sound design and the ability to move between songs, stage work and larger narrative forms.

show-gray-brothers.bio: Broome-raised brothers Albert and Elwood Gray make folk-alt-country built around blood harmonies, crafted lyrics, guitar/mandolin interplay and relaxed stage chemistry.
show-gray-brothers.why: Useful if you want a songwriting and harmony break from the heavier acts; the sibling vocal blend and sparse arrangements are the main draw for you.

show-blush.bio: Boorloo four-piece Blush bring gloomy, ferocious indie rock and punk energy, with references around Mannequin Pussy, Hole and Wet Leg.
show-blush.why: High recommendation. The darker edge, distorted rock dynamics and abrasive live energy are close to the more aggressive side of your own taste.

show-tchega.bio: Tchéga, led by Réunion-born singer-songwriter Carole Katz, blends Creole folk and roots with sega, maloya and Indian Ocean rhythms in an upbeat full-band setting.
show-tchega.why: A genre detour for you, but valuable for rhythmic ideas, cultural fusion and seeing a band create a strong musical identity without relying on rock conventions.

show-jj-vacant.bio: JJ Vacant is a young Noongar/Wongi and Pitjantjatjara hip-hop artist from Boorloo, known for rapid-fire flow, sharp lyricism and high-energy contemporary production.
show-jj-vacant.why: Not a direct genre match, but worthwhile if you want ideas around rhythmic vocal delivery, lyrical economy and modern production architecture.

show-clare-perrott.bio: Clare Perrott is a Boorloo folk-rock songwriter combining intricate guitar writing, emotionally direct songs and a full-band sound influenced by artists such as Adrianne Lenker, Jeff Buckley and Fleetwood Mac.
show-clare-perrott.why: Strong songwriting pick for you, particularly for chord movement, guitar arrangement and emotionally effective full-band dynamics outside your heavier material.

show-heaven-alone.bio: Perth heavy-alt-rock band heaven // alone blend metal and hardcore weight with ambient, experimental and shoegaze-like textures.
show-heaven-alone.why: Top recommendation and probably the closest match on the bill to your dark/heavy taste. The metal-hardcore foundation plus atmosphere and production experimentation should be especially relevant.

show-lightnin-jack.bio: South West veteran Lightnin Jack makes raw blues-rock built around gravelly vocals, slide/lap guitar, foot percussion and a stripped-back, highly physical live approach.
show-lightnin-jack.why: A good musicianship pick for you: fewer layers, but strong guitar tone, rhythmic independence and a one-person/full-band sense of momentum worth studying.

show-georga-raath.bio: Fremantle artist-producer Georga Raath makes emotionally charged alternative pop with cinematic electronic production, intimate vocals and self-produced arrangements.
show-georga-raath.why: Useful for your production and soundtrack interests: pay attention to atmosphere, vocal space and how cinematic texture can carry a relatively compact pop song.

show-forever-party.bio: The Forever Party pair introspective alt-rock with explosive dynamics, sweeping strings, four-part harmonies and cathartic live arrangements.
show-forever-party.why: Near-top recommendation. Their mix of big rock release, detailed arrangement, harmony and strings lines up strongly with your taste for anthemic, expansive and almost operatic music.

show-ratsalad.bio: Geraldton trio RATSALAD. are a loud, high-energy pub-punk band whose recent material crosses punk, hardcore, grunge and metal.
show-ratsalad.why: Near-top recommendation. This is the most direct route to the fast, loud, hardcore side of your taste; go for energy, riffs and how a three-piece creates maximum impact.

show-odlaw.bio: Boorloo collective Odlaw build indie rock around Mark Neal's songwriting, mixing lo-fi bedroom-punk attitude with a large, flexible ensemble and deliberately unorthodox arrangements.
show-odlaw.why: Interesting for your collaborative/arrangement side: less heavy, but the loose collective format and willingness to reshape songs could give you useful production ideas.

show-little-guilt.bio: Perth five-piece Little Guilt make polished indie-pop that moves between rock instrumentation and electronic touches, with a strong live following since forming in 2021.
show-little-guilt.why: More polished indie than your core taste, but potentially useful for hook construction, contemporary arrangement and translating recorded pop into a full-band show.

show-claudia-tripp.bio: Perth singer-songwriter Claudia Tripp is a country-pop artist known for powerhouse vocals, catchy melodies and direct, relatable songwriting.
show-claudia-tripp.why: Not a close genre fit, but worth considering if you want to study concise hooks, vocal delivery and professional pop-country songcraft.
